_comment: GLOBAL SAFETY CEILING. This file is the trust anchor: it lives in the global OpenCode config, not in any project. A project's .orchestrator/policy.json can only NARROW this. It can never raise it. lib/policy.py enforces that arithmetically via effective = min(ceiling, project_class).
_ceiling_rationale: Permits trial/limited-time endpoints for public and disposable workloads, which is what makes free models usable for testing orchestration mechanics. Forbids training-explicit entirely, so no project can opt into a model that trains on its prompts.
_default_rationale: Absent an explicit project declaration, assume the stricter class. A missing or unreadable project file must never loosen protection, so the default is 'private' rather than 'disposable'.

private.use_for: Any repository that is not public, or that contains code, credentials, customer data, or personal data.

public.use_for: Code that is already public and contains nothing sensitive.

disposable.use_for: Synthetic fixtures and throwaway sandboxes only. Still bounded by safety_ceiling above.

enforcement.no_permitted_route: fail closed; the worker exits 3 rather than selecting an ineligible route
enforcement.unparsable_project_policy: ignored; the global ceiling and default class apply
